purpose: Map the revised paper's claims to executable analyses and recorded evidence. Paths are relative to the project root; numerical values remain in the linked result tables.
scope: The manuscript reports a numerical coexistence result at p=alpha=1/2. The infinite-time voter endpoint, exact orientation independence, asymptotic wetting exponent and controlled d=2 matching theory are not established.

items.claim: Exactly two absorbing configurations for p>0 in the studied model
items.qualification: Analytic proof. The finite-system recurrence argument additionally uses strictly interior nonzero flip probabilities; p=0 has extra frozen states.

items.claim: Exponentially many frozen configurations at p=0
items.qualification: Explicit independent 2x2 checkerboard-block switches prove N_frozen >= 2^(LxLy/16) for lengths divisible by 4. Fixed-width transfer matrices estimate strip entropies only.

items.claim: Front reversal and its orientation, time-window and threshold dependence
items.qualification: Every published parameter/window retains all declared seeds with complete valid geometry. Sampling intervals are separate from threshold, interpolation, temporal and orientation effects. T2M, T5M and independent axial T10M cohorts remain separate; unresolved shifts do not establish equivalence.

items.claim: Persistent bulk activity and finite-size lifetime contrast near the flagship transition
items.qualification: Unconditional complete ensembles, run-wise time integration, known absorbed extensions and explicit censoring. Half-density crossing differs from consensus. Finite-time lifetime observations do not determine an asymptotic growth law.

items.claim: Direct spatial correlations in the large active systems
items.qualification: Final configurations from complete cohorts only, with SHA and global-observable checks. Exact ensemble spin symmetry gives zero mean. Signed long-distance fluctuations and pointwise independent-run intervals are retained; no exponent or correlation-length extrapolation is inferred.

items.claim: Droplet growth, curvature and complementary droplets of the two phases
items.qualification: Success is boundary growth before extinction and before the declared horizon, not infinite-time survival. No interval with both droplets shrinking is resolved at the actual sampled probabilities; an arbitrarily narrow interval is not excluded.

items.claim: Increasing active adsorption at a wall and the ambiguity of a wetting exponent
items.qualification: All 28 new wall runs are complete with matched-size baselines and valid geometry. The closest point resolves a roughly 4.5% size difference and weak late drift. Legacy fits retain their disclosed selection and baseline limits. Joint forecasts use one common front-derived reference, with sampling covariance and reference sensitivity kept separate; no asymptotic exponent or size convergence is claimed.

items.claim: Long crossovers and the unresolved order near the voter endpoint
items.qualification: The L8192 q=.000640 ensemble declines through 20M with one consensus event; midpoint q=.000642 persists but retains late drift. A front requires a separated band with interpretable interior activity. Finite-time seed suppression does not universally exclude GV criticality, and sampled-active-point magnetic ratios do not determine the boundary universality.

The separately declared primary 8M confirmation is complete: all 16 fixed 500k shards, with adaptive stopping disabled, disjoint RNG keys and output/checkpoint agreement. The original 16M cohort remains separate. Local exponent windows require at least 20 surviving replicas and do not establish an asymptotic law.

items.claim: Higher-lineage terms permit bistability in an exact finite-cutoff reaction calculation
items.qualification: Exact identities refer to the stated finite-time voter reference law. Physical matching is an approximation, its time-scale sensitivity is not a confidence interval, and checkpoint histograms lack the cross-time covariance needed for independent-point extrapolation.

items.claim: Dense CPU/GPU trajectory equivalence and reproducible completion
items.qualification: Each production worker validates before running. Completion includes parameter, scheduled-record, profile, final-time and final-state digest checks. GPU absorption is interval observed; sparse replicas and precise lifetimes use CPU.

items.claim: Five-cell comparison distinguishes boundary prediction from unresolved transition order
items.qualification: The four resolved disk half-survival radii use T=20000 and adaptive survivor-target sampling. All escapes are zero. A fifth parameter pair supplies only a radius lower bound. Initial small-seed decay is not asymptotic linear stability.

Legacy profile cuts and parameter-fit sensitivity are retained explicitly; eta examples are individual trajectories. Lazy late seed plateaus contain boundary escapes and adaptively stopped samples. Finite-r checks do not establish the continuous-time limit. The p=.5 lazy crossing is reanalyzed with the corrected envelope and explicit physical-time windows; its ratio is reported only as approximately .86.
